license_note: The Upstage Solar License adopts the grants of the Apache License 2.0, including commercial use, and adds Section 4(e): anyone who distributes or makes available a model created, trained, fine-tuned, or otherwise improved using the weights must begin its name with "Solar", prominently display "Built with Solar", and provide the license alongside it. Upstage's announcement confirms that commercial use and derivative models through fine-tuning and distillation are permitted. A naming and branding condition on every derivative model departs from an open-source posture, so the release is source-available rather than open source.

license_evidence.scope: upstage/Solar-Open2-250B weights, configuration, tokenizer, and documentation, and any derivative AI model created, trained, fine-tuned, or otherwise improved using them. The NotaAI quantizations are published in separate repositories.

access_boundary: This record represents the upstage/Solar-Open2-250B release announced July 22, 2026. The predecessor Solar Open 100B, the NotaAI INT4, INT4-GlobalPruned, and NVFP4 quantizations, Upstage's forks of Transformers and vLLM, the proprietary Solar Pro and Solar Mini API models, and the Upstage Playground trial that ended July 31, 2026 remain separate boundaries.
strengths: Developer-published BF16 safetensors checkpoint on the Upstage Hugging Face organization, with the technical report and license file in the same repository and official NotaAI INT4 and NVFP4 quantizations linked from the model card

First-party model card documents the architecture, parameter counts, context length, training tokens and hardware, reasoning modes, tool-call parsing, and Transformers and vLLM serving paths, including connecting Claude Code and Hermes Agent to a local server
tradeoffs: The Upstage Solar License requires every distributed derivative model to begin its name with "Solar" and to display "Built with Solar"

Serving depends on Upstage's forks of Transformers and vLLM on NVIDIA GPUs, and the documented examples assume eight GPUs with at least 141 GB each; no developer API or third-party hosted path is documented
No versioning or deprecation posture is stated for the Solar Open line
